lessons.title: Singing a song with the right tune
lessons.objective: Sing songs with correct tones and melody, and show respect when the national anthem is sung.
lessons.course:
To sing well, we listen to the tune, we breathe at the end of a line and we pronounce each word clearly.
The national anthem is sung on important occasions. We stand still, we sing it with pride and we do not talk or move. (The words are learnt with the teacher from the official text.)

support.title: Klassia playground song
support.text:
Come and play, come and play,
skip the rope and run away,
when the bell rings, line up straight,
never push and never wait!

lessons.model: The adult sings the song slowly, breathing at the end of each line.
lessons.guided: Learn the song line by line. Sing it in two groups: one sings a line, the other answers with the next.
lessons.exercise: What do we do when the national anthem is sung?
lessons.answer: We stand still and sing with pride.
accept: We stand still and sing with pride
lessons.remediation: Sing the first two lines several times before the rest.
lessons.transfer: Teach the song to a younger child.
lessons.materials: Your voice; the official text of the anthem from the teacher.

practice.prompt: Listen to the song and sing it after the voice.
practice.listen: Come and play, come and play, skip the rope and run away, when the bell rings, line up straight, never push and never wait!
practice.answer: The song sung with the tune.
practice.explanation: Breathe at the end of each line.

practice.prompt: Which word rhymes with “play”?
practice.answer: away

practice.prompt: When do we breathe while singing?
practice.answer: At the end of a line.
accept: at the end of a line
at the end of each line
At the end of a line
practice.explanation: Breathing at the end of a line keeps the tune.

lessons.title: A cartoon strip and its moral
lessons.objective: Read a cartoon strip, put oneself in the place of a character and deduce the moral.
lessons.course: A cartoon tells a story in boxes with drawings and speech bubbles. We read the boxes from left to right, top to bottom, and we look at the faces to understand feelings.

support.title: Klassia cartoon (four boxes)
support.text:
Box 1: Ekane: “I am the best footballer! Nobody can take the ball from me!”
Box 2: Ekane dribbles alone and refuses to pass the ball to his team.
Box 3: Three players from the other team surround him and take the ball. They score.
Box 4: Ekane, sad: “Next time, I will pass the ball. A team wins together.”

lessons.model: The adult reads box 1 with a proud voice and box 4 with a sad voice, then asks how Ekane changed.
lessons.guided: Read the four boxes. Act them in a group. Say what Ekane learnt.
lessons.exercise: What does Ekane learn at the end?
lessons.answer: A team wins together, so he must pass the ball.
accept: A team wins together, so he must pass the ball
lessons.remediation: Read box by box with the adult and describe each face.
lessons.transfer: Draw a four-box cartoon about a game you play.
lessons.materials: The cartoon (text version); paper to draw.

practice.prompt: Put the boxes in order.
items: Ekane says he is the best.
The other team takes the ball.
He decides to pass next time.
practice.answer: best, refuses, loses the ball, decides to pass.

practice.prompt: How does Ekane feel in box 4?
practice.answer: sad

practice.prompt: Draw a four-box cartoon about a game.
practice.answer: A cartoon in four boxes.

lessons.title: Spelling: the apostrophe s’ for plural owners
lessons.objective: Use the apostrophe after s (s’) to show that something belongs to several people.
lessons.course:
When a plural noun ends in s, we add only an apostrophe to show owning: the boys’ ball (the ball of the boys), the players’ shirts, my parents’ room.
Compare: the girl’s skipping rope (one girl) — the girls’ skipping rope (many girls).
lessons.model: The adult writes: “the ball of the boys” → “the boys’ ball”; “the whistle of the referee” → “the referee’s whistle”.
lessons.guided: Sort phrases: one owner (’s) or many owners (s’). Then rewrite them.
lessons.exercise: Write with an apostrophe: the shirts of the players.
lessons.remediation: Draw one owner and many owners to see the difference.
lessons.transfer: Write three phrases about your family with s’ (my parents’ house, my sisters’ room).

practice.prompt: Complete with ’s or s’.
practice.text: the girl[[’s]] rope (one girl); the team[[s’]] flags (two teams)
practice.answer: the girl’s rope; the teams’ flags.
practice.explanation: One owner: ’s. Many owners ending in s: s’.

practice.prompt: Which one means “the ball of the boys”?
practice.answer: the boys’ ball

practice.prompt: Write: the house of my parents.
practice.answer: my parents’ house

lessons.title: Adverbs and interjections in games
lessons.objective: Use adverbs of manner, place and time, and interjections to express feelings.
lessons.course:
Adverbs tell more about a verb. Manner (how): quickly, slowly, carefully, well. Place (where): here, there, outside, everywhere. Time (when): now, today, yesterday, soon.
Interjections express feelings and are followed by an exclamation mark: Hurray! Bravo! Hey! Oh!
lessons.model: The adult commentates a race: “Tabi runs quickly! He is there now! Hurray! He wins! Bravo, Tabi!”
lessons.guided: Commentate a game in pairs using three adverbs and two interjections.
lessons.exercise: Complete with an adverb of manner: Manka skips ___ (in a careful way).
lessons.remediation: Practise adverbs of manner with -ly first (slow → slowly).
lessons.transfer: Describe how your friends play, using adverbs.
lessons.materials: A ball or a rope for the game.

practice.prompt: Match each adverb with its kind.
practice.answer: quickly: manner; outside: place; yesterday: time.
practice.explanation: Adverbs tell how, where or when.

practice.prompt: Which interjection shows joy for a winner?
practice.answer: Hurray!

practice.prompt: Complete.
practice.text: The players ran [[slowly]] (slow) because they were tired.
practice.answer: slowly

lessons.title: The circle: centre, radius and diameter
lessons.objective: Describe the centre, radius and diameter of a circle and draw circles.
lessons.course:
Every point of a circle is at the same distance from the centre. The radius goes from the centre to the circle. The diameter crosses the circle through the centre: it is twice the radius.
We can draw a circle with a string fixed at the centre, or with a compass.
lessons.model: On the playground, the adult draws a big circle for a game with a stick tied to a rope of 2 m: radius 2 m, diameter 4 m.
lessons.guided: Draw a circle with a string and a pencil. Mark the centre, draw a radius and a diameter, and measure them.
lessons.exercise: The radius of a circle is 6 cm. What is the diameter?
lessons.remediation: Fold a paper circle in two to see the diameter.
lessons.transfer: Find circles in games and objects at home (a ball, a plate, a tyre).
lessons.materials: String, pencil, compass (with an adult), ruler.

practice.prompt: The diameter is 10 cm. What is the radius in cm?
practice.explanation: The radius is half the diameter.

practice.prompt: Which line goes through the centre from one side to the other?
practice.answer: the diameter
practice.explanation: The diameter crosses through the centre.

practice.prompt: Draw a circle and mark its centre, a radius and a diameter.
practice.answer: A circle with centre, radius and diameter.

lessons.title: Solid shapes in games
lessons.objective: Recognise and describe solid (3D) shapes: cube, cuboid, cylinder, sphere, cone and pyramid.
lessons.course: Solid shapes have faces, edges and corners (vertices). A cube has 6 square faces. A cuboid has 6 rectangular faces. A cylinder has 2 circular faces (a tin). A sphere is round (a ball). A cone has 1 circular face and a point.
lessons.model: The adult shows game objects: a dice (cube), a ball (sphere), a tin used as a drum (cylinder).
lessons.guided: Collect objects at home and sort them by shape. Count the faces of a box.
lessons.exercise: How many faces has a cube?
lessons.remediation: Work with three shapes first: cube, sphere, cylinder.
lessons.transfer: Make a cone with paper for a party hat.

practice.prompt: Match each object with its shape.
practice.answer: dice: cube; football: sphere; tin: cylinder.

practice.prompt: Which shape has a point and one circular face?
practice.answer: cone

practice.prompt: How many edges does a cube have?

lessons.title: Building shapes with local materials
lessons.objective: Construct shapes using natural and recycled materials and solve shape puzzles.
lessons.course:
We can build shapes with sticks, straws, bottle tops and cartons: a triangle with 3 sticks, a square with 4 equal sticks, a cube with 12 sticks and clay balls at the corners.
A tangram is a puzzle of 7 pieces that make many figures.
lessons.model: The adult makes a cube frame with 12 sticks and 8 small balls of clay.
lessons.guided: Build a triangle, a square and a cube frame. Then make a figure with paper tangram pieces.
lessons.exercise: How many sticks are needed for a cube frame?
lessons.remediation: Build flat shapes before solid ones.
lessons.transfer: Build a small house frame with sticks and show your family.
lessons.materials: Sticks or straws, clay, paper for a tangram.

practice.prompt: How many corners (vertices) does a cube have?
Which shape can we make with 3 sticks?
practice.answer: triangle

practice.prompt: Draw the figure you made with the tangram.
practice.answer: A drawing of the tangram figure.

lessons.title: Number bonds of 5, 6 and 7 in games
lessons.objective: Make number bonds of 5, 6 and 7 quickly and use them in mental calculation.
lessons.course:
Number bonds are pairs of numbers that make a total. Bonds of 7: 0 + 7, 1 + 6, 2 + 5, 3 + 4.
They help us calculate fast: 37 + 3 → think 7 + 3 = 10, so 40.
lessons.model: In a game of songo, the adult splits 7 seeds into two holes in all possible ways: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, 3 and 4.
lessons.guided: Play “hidden hand”: hide some of 6 seeds in one hand, the friend says how many are hidden.
lessons.remediation: Use seeds to make each bond.
lessons.transfer: Play the hidden hand game with a friend.

practice.prompt: Match the pairs that make 6.
Complete.

lessons.title: States of matter and safe drinking water
lessons.objective: Describe the three states of matter, associate sources of water with their uses and explain what makes water safe to drink.
lessons.course:
Matter exists in three states: solid (ice, stone), liquid (water, oil) and gas (steam, air). Water can change: ice melts into water, water boils into steam.
Sources of water: rain, streams, rivers, wells, boreholes, taps. Potable water is clean, has no smell, no colour and no germs. We can boil or filter water to make it safer, and we drink water regularly, especially after playing.
lessons.model: The adult heats water in a pot: “The liquid becomes steam, a gas.” Then shows ice melting in the sun.
lessons.guided: Sort objects into solids, liquids and gases. Filter muddy water with sand and cloth (it looks clearer, but it still needs boiling).
lessons.exercise: What is water when it is frozen?
lessons.remediation: Observe ice, water and steam with the adult.
lessons.transfer: Drink a glass of clean water after playing every day.
lessons.materials: Ice, a pot, water, a clean cloth, sand (with an adult).

practice.prompt: Match each thing with its state.
practice.answer: stone: solid; oil: liquid; steam: gas.
practice.explanation: There are three states of matter.

practice.prompt: Which water is safest to drink?
practice.answer: boiled and cooled water

practice.prompt: Water boils and becomes steam. Which state is steam?
practice.answer: Gas.
practice.explanation: Steam is water as a gas.

lessons.title: Combien coûte le ballon ?
lessons.objective: Demander un prix, exprimer un souhait poliment et compter jusqu’à 1 000 dans un achat.
lessons.course:
Pour demander un prix : « Combien coûte le ballon ? » « C’est combien ? » On répond : « Ça coûte cinq cents francs. »
Pour exprimer un souhait : « Je veux… », « J’ai envie de… », « Je voudrais…, s’il vous plaît. »
Nombres : cent (100), deux cents (200), cinq cents (500), mille (1 000).

support.title: Jeu de rôle
support.text:
— Bonjour, monsieur. Combien coûte le ballon ?
— Ça coûte cinq cents francs.
— Je voudrais un ballon, s’il vous plaît.
— Voilà. Merci !

lessons.model: Au marché, Tabi demande poliment le prix d’une corde à sauter et l’achète.
lessons.guided: Joue la scène d’achat avec des prix en français. Change les objets et les prix.
lessons.remediation: Travaille d’abord « Combien ? » avec des étiquettes de prix.
lessons.transfer: Au marché avec un adulte, écoute les prix et répète-les en français.
lessons.materials: Étiquettes de prix, objets ou images.

practice.prompt: Relie les nombres.
practice.answer: 100 cent ; 500 cinq cents ; 1 000 mille.

practice.prompt: Quelle phrase est polie ?
choices: Je voudrais un ballon, s’il vous plaît.
practice.answer: Je voudrais un ballon, s’il vous plaît.
practice.explanation: « Je voudrais… s’il vous plaît » est poli.

practice.prompt: Écoute et répète la scène.
practice.listen: Bonjour, monsieur. Combien coûte le ballon ? Ça coûte cinq cents francs. Je voudrais un ballon, s’il vous plaît.
practice.answer: La scène répétée.
practice.explanation: Joue la scène avec un partenaire.

lessons.title: Apologising, honesty and appreciation in games
lessons.objective: Practise universal values in games: apologising, honesty, respect and appreciation.
lessons.course: In games and in life, we show values: we apologise when we hurt someone (“I am sorry”), we are honest (we do not cheat), we respect the rules and the other players, and we appreciate others (“Well played!”).
lessons.model: During a match, Ekane pushes Neba by mistake. He stops, helps him up and says: “I am sorry.”
lessons.guided: Act situations: a mistake, a cheat, a good move. Say the right words for each one.
lessons.exercise: You push a friend by mistake. What do you say?
lessons.remediation: Practise one value at a time with a short role play.
lessons.transfer: Say “Well played!” to a friend after a game this week.

practice.prompt: Match each situation with the value.
pairs: You say sorry after a mistake.
practice.answer: apology; honesty; appreciation.

practice.prompt: Which one is honest?
choices: saying the ball went out when it did
practice.answer: saying the ball went out when it did

practice.prompt: Say one way to show respect to the other team.
practice.answer: Shake hands and say well played.

lessons.title: Moulding toys with the right quantities
lessons.objective: Prepare a moulding mixture with the right quantities and mould objects for games.
lessons.course:
To mould well, we mix the right quantities. For salt dough: 2 cups of flour, 1 cup of salt, about 1 cup of water. Too much water makes it sticky; too little makes it crack.
We can mould marbles, little animals or pieces for a board game, then let them dry.
lessons.model: The adult measures 2 cups of flour and 1 cup of salt, adds water little by little and kneads.
lessons.guided: Prepare the dough with the right quantities. Mould pieces for a board game and let them dry.
lessons.exercise: How many cups of flour for 1 cup of salt?
lessons.remediation: Use ready dough first and practise shapes.
lessons.transfer: Mould a set of game pieces and play with your family.
lessons.materials: Flour, salt, water, cups, a board.

practice.prompt: If we use 4 cups of flour, how many cups of salt?
The dough is sticky. What did we add too much of?
practice.answer: water
practice.explanation: Too much water makes it sticky.

practice.prompt: Draw the pieces you moulded.
practice.answer: A drawing of the game pieces.

lessons.title: Painting a landscape and talking about it
lessons.objective: Paint a landscape with appropriate colours and appreciate beauty in paintings.
lessons.course:
A landscape shows the land: the sky, the hills, trees, a river, houses. Far things are small and near things are big.
To appreciate a painting we say what we see, the colours, and what we like: “I like the bright green of the trees.”
lessons.model: The adult paints a sky in blue, hills in green and a red road, then says what she likes.
lessons.guided: Paint the landscape around your house. Show it and say two things you like in a friend’s painting.
lessons.exercise: In a landscape, are far trees big or small?
lessons.remediation: Paint only the sky and the ground first.
lessons.transfer: Make an exhibition of family drawings at home.

practice.prompt: Paint or draw a landscape.
practice.answer: A landscape with sky, land and trees.
practice.explanation: Near things big, far things small.

practice.prompt: Which sentence appreciates a painting?
choices: I like the bright colours of the sky.
I do not look at it.
practice.answer: I like the bright colours of the sky.
practice.explanation: We say what we like politely.

practice.prompt: Say one thing you like in a painting.
practice.answer: For example: I like the colours of the river.

lessons.title: Team sports: passing the ball in handball
lessons.objective: Pass and catch a ball in a team game and respect the rules and the referee.
lessons.course:
Team sports: football, handball, volleyball, basketball. In handball, we pass the ball with the hands, we do not walk more than three steps with the ball, we shoot at the goal.
To pass: look at your teammate, throw to the chest; to catch: hands open, eyes on the ball.
lessons.model: The adult passes the ball to the chest of a child and says: “Look, throw, catch!”
lessons.guided: Pass the ball ten times with a partner. Play a small game: three players against three.
lessons.exercise: How many steps can you take with the ball in handball?
lessons.remediation: Pass and catch at a short distance first.
lessons.transfer: Play a team game with friends and respect the rules.

practice.prompt: Match each sport with how we play the ball.
practice.answer: football: feet; handball: hands; volleyball: net.

practice.prompt: The referee whistles a foul. What do you do?
practice.answer: stop and respect the decision

practice.prompt: Your team scores 3 goals, the other team 2. By how many goals do you win?

lessons.title: Reading and writing numbers 1 to 30 in the family language
lessons.objective: Read and write simple words and numbers from 1 to 30 in the family language with an adult.
lessons.course:
Each language has its way of counting. In many languages, numbers above ten are built from smaller numbers (for example “ten and one”).
With an adult who speaks the language, we say, read and write numbers from 1 to 30, then short messages of two sentences.
lessons.model: The adult counts objects from 1 to 10 in the family language, then explains how 11 and 20 are built.
lessons.guided: Count 30 stones with an adult in the family language. Write the numbers 1 to 10 with the adult, then two short sentences.
lessons.exercise: How many numbers do we learn in this lesson?
lessons.transfer: Count things at home in the family language every day.
lessons.materials: 30 stones or seeds, paper, an adult.

practice.prompt: Write the numbers 1 to 10 in the family language with an adult.
practice.answer: Numbers written with the adult.

practice.prompt: Write a message of two sentences in the family language with an adult.
practice.answer: A short message of two sentences.

lessons.title: The word processor toolbar: bold, size, colour
lessons.objective: Identify the main buttons of a word processor toolbar and format a short text.
lessons.course: A word processor is a program to write and decorate texts. On the toolbar: B makes text bold, I makes it italic, U underlines; we can change the size and the colour of letters, and align the text left, centre or right. Save keeps the work.
lessons.model: The adult types a title, selects it, clicks B and makes it bigger and centred.
lessons.guided: With an adult, type the title “My school”, make it bold, bigger and centred, then save.
lessons.remediation: Use only B and the size first.
lessons.transfer: Make a small title page for a school project with an adult.
lessons.materials: A computer with a word processor (with an adult).

practice.prompt: Match each button with its effect.
practice.answer: B: bold; I: italic; U: underline.

practice.prompt: What must we do before changing the style of a word?
practice.answer: select it

practice.prompt: Why do we save our work?
practice.answer: To keep it and find it later.
